division.heading: Reasons the Minister may refuse to process an application for an Australian travel document

section.heading: Reasons relating to fraud or dishonesty in application for Australian travel document

content.p: The Minister may refuse to process an application for an Australian travel document if the Minister suspects, on reasonable grounds, that:
a statement made in, or in connection with, the application:
is false or misleading; or
omits any matter or thing without which the statement is misleading; or
information given in, or in connection with, the application:
is false or misleading; or
omits any matter or thing without which the information is misleading; or
a document given in, or in connection with, the application is false or misleading.
If the Minister refuses to process the application, the applicable fee (if any) accompanying the application is not refundable.
If the Minister refuses to process the application and the person concerned still wishes that an Australian travel document be issued, a fresh application is required under section 7 or 9.
This section does not limit section 29, 30 or 31.

section.heading: When Australian travel documents are not valid

content.p: Cessation of validity
An Australian travel document ceases to be valid:
in accordance with a determination made for the purposes of subsection (2); or
at the time specified on the document; or
when cancelled under this Division;
whichever happens first.
A Minister’s determination may specify the time at which, or circumstances in which, an Australian travel document ceases to be valid.
Suspension of validity
An Australian travel document is not valid while it is suspended under section 22A.

section.heading: Possessing false Australian travel documents

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person has possession or control of a document; and
the person knows that the document is a false Australian travel document.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 1,000 penalty units, or both.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Note: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2). See subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Repeal the sections, substitute:

section.heading: Selling a genuine or false Australian travel document

content.p: A person commits an offence if the person sells an Australian travel document or a false Australian travel document.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 1,000 penalty units, or both.

section.heading: Damaging or interfering with an Australian travel document

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person engages in conduct in relation to an Australian travel document; and
the conduct results in:
the destruction of the Australian travel document; or
damage to, manipulation of, or tampering or interference with the Australian travel document; or
damage to, manipulation of, or tampering or interference with the Australian travel document’s contactless integrated circuit; or
the removal of the Australian travel document’s contactless integrated circuit.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 1,000 penalty units, or both.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Note: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (2). See subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Repeal the section, substitute:

section.heading: Making or providing false Australian travel documents

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person makes a false Australian travel document; and
the person does so with the intention that the document may be used, acted upon or accepted as if it were an Australian travel document.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 1,000 penalty units, or both.
A person commits an offence if:
the person provides a false Australian travel document to another person; and
the person does so with the intention that the document may be used, acted upon or accepted as if it were an Australian travel document.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 10 years or 1,000 penalty units, or both.
Paragraph (2)(a) does not apply if the person has a reasonable excuse.
Note: The defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (3). See subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
